Operation Log – Sundari Translocation Operation
Operation log

11:15 – Visual observation from ridge (binoculars, ~400m). Sundari accompanied by two subadult males. Noted minor limp in left foreleg – likely old injury, no new wound. Vet (Dr. Meera) consulted remotely; advised no intervention unless limping worsens.

12:00 – Break. Water and ration distribution. Team morale good.

12:45 – Route reconnaissance for drive: planned route from Kothur ford to Yadavalli clearing. Distance ~8 km, terrain moderate. Two potential bottlenecks identified: narrow gorge at mile 3, and dry stream bed at mile 6.5 (soft sand, risk of vehicle bogging).

13:30 – Return to base. Vehicle T-2 tire pressure checked. All good.

14:20 – Radio message from Range Officer (Nallamala West): reported fresh pugmarks near Yadavalli, possibly male elephant. Noted for tomorrow's briefing.

15:00 – Equipment storage. Collar S-17 placed on charger (backup). S-14 left on bench for final calibration.

15:40 – Status update: ACTIVE. All systems nominal. No deviations.

16:10 – AR signs off for the day. Next update scheduled 06:00, 09 Aug.

---

09 Aug 2026

05:55 – Team assembly. Weather: overcast, 22°C, humidity high. Rain likely by afternoon.

06:10 – Pre-drive briefing. Objective: move Sundari (and any accompanying subadults) from Kothur valley to Yadavalli clearing. Capture team to use soft nets; darting only if necessary. Vet on standby at clearing.

06:40 – Vehicle T-2 loaded. T-1 left at base for radiator repair (Ramesh to source replacement hose).

07:00 – Departure. ETA at Kothur ford: 07:45.

07:50 – Arrived at ford. Water level rising (overnight rain upstream). Crossing delayed – waiting for water to subside. Team on standby.

08:30 – Water level still high. Estimated wait: 1–2 hours. Minor delay, no action required.

09:15 – Crossing attempted. T-2 made it across; T-1 (still at base) not needed. Capture team on foot forded with equipment. All personnel safe.

09:50 – Telemetry lock on Sundari. Position: 15.2389°N, 78.4581°E. Moving west, towards Yadavalli. Subadults with her.

In the operation log, Arjun Rao recorded that the Sundari Translocation Operation status is interrupted. Record status: current.

10:30 – Visual contact. Sundari resting under banyan tree, ~300m from planned drive path. Subadults grazing nearby. No disturbance.

11:15 – Drive initiated. Capture team formed loose arc, advancing slowly. Sundari alert but not fleeing. Subadults moving with her.

12:00 – Drive progressing. Sundari moved ~1.5 km west, towards clearing. Pace steady.

12:45 – Radio check. All teams in position. Dr. Meera at clearing, ready.

13:20 – Sundari entered Yadavalli clearing. Capture team closing in.

14:05 – STATUS CHANGE: INTERRUPTED.

Reason: Sudden thunderstorm with lightning. Operations halted for safety. All personnel retreated to vehicles. Sundari and subadults moved to dense cover at clearing edge. No injuries, no equipment loss.

14:30 – Storm passed. Resumed assessment. Sundari still in clearing, but agitated. Subadults separated – one moved north, one stayed with her.

15:00 – Decision: abort drive for today. Sundari too stressed after storm. Subadult separation complicates capture. Team to regroup at base, reassess tomorrow.

15:40 – Return to base. All equipment accounted for. Collar S-14 telemetry still functional; S-17 backup not used.

16:20 – Status update: INTERRUPTED. Notes: storm disruption, subadult separation, Sundari stress level high. Next action: monitor overnight, reassess 06:00, 10 Aug.

16:45 – AR signs off. Dr. Meera to remain on call.

---

10 Aug 2026

05:50 – Team assembly. Weather: clear, 20°C, calm. Good conditions.

06:00 – Telemetry check. Sundari's position: 15.2450°N, 78.4655°E – moved back towards Kothur valley overnight. Subadult (north) at 15.2520°N, 78.4700°E; other subadult with Sundari.

06:30 – Briefing. Plan: re-attempt drive, but with modified approach – use two capture teams, one for Sundari, one for subadult if separation occurs. Vet to monitor stress levels.

07:00 – Departure. Vehicle T-2, plus T-1 (radiator hose replaced, test run successful).
10 Aug 2026 (continued)

07:15 – Departure delayed. T-1 reported low brake fluid on pre-drive check. Fluid topped up, leak checked – no visible issue. 15 min delay.

07:30 – En route to Kothur valley. Weather holding.

08:10 – Arrived at staging point. Telemetry: Sundari at 15.2465°N, 78.4630°E, still moving slowly west. Subadult (north) at 15.2530°N, 78.4715°E. Other subadult with Sundari.

08:45 – Briefing with team. Two-team approach confirmed. Team A (Ravi, Suresh, Lakshmi) for Sundari. Team B (Kavya, Irfan, Dev) for subadult if separation. Dr. Meera to observe from ridge with binoculars, radio contact every 15 min.

09:20 – Drive started. Sundari moving west along valley edge. Pace moderate. Subadult with her.

09:50 – Radio: Sundari stopped at stream crossing. Drinking. Team A holding position 200m behind. No stress indicators.

10:15 – Sundari crossed stream. Moving north-east now, away from planned capture zone. Team A adjusting.

10:40 – Subadult (north) started moving south, towards Sundari. Team B on alert.

11:05 – Subadult rejoined Sundari. Both moving together now. Good – separation resolved on its own.

11:30 – Sundari entered secondary clearing, ~4 ha, good visibility. Team A closing.

12:00 – STATUS: CAPTURE ATTEMPT IN PROGRESS. Sundari in clearing, subadults both with her. Dr. Meera reports calm behavior – feeding on grass, no agitation.

12:25 – Capture team moved in. Sundari stood up, alert. Team held position.

12:40 – Sundari moved to clearing edge, looked back at team, then walked into dense cover. Subadults followed. Capture attempt failed – no dart fired.

13:00 – Team regrouped. Discussion: Sundari aware of presence, but not fleeing far. She is holding territory, not stressed. Dr. Meera: "She knows we're here. She's not afraid, just cautious. We need a different approach."

13:30 – Decision: switch to bait-corral method. Use existing corral at Yadavalli clearing (checked 5 Aug, structure sound). Bait with fodder and minerals. Sundari has used this clearing before – familiar.

14:00 – Corral prep. Team B to Yadavalli. Team A to monitor Sundari from distance.

14:30 – Bait placed. Fodder, salt block, water. Corral gate left open, will close remotely.

15:00 – Sundari's position: 15.2480°N, 78.4665°E – moving slowly towards Yadavalli. Promising.

15:30 – Radio check. All teams in position. Dr. Meera at ridge, observing.

16:00 – Sundari at clearing edge, ~150m from corral. Feeding. Subadults nearby.

16:30 – Sundari entered corral. Gate closed remotely. SUCCESS. Capture complete.

16:45 – Vet team entered corral. Sundari sedated. Collar S-14 replaced with new GPS collar (S-18). Blood samples taken. Body condition good – weight 185 kg, no injuries.

17:15 – Subadults moved away from corral, into adjacent forest. Monitoring continues. They are not distressed – Dr. Meera observed them feeding within 30 min.

17:30 – Sundari loaded for transport. Vehicle T-3 (transport crate) confirmed ready.

18:00 – Transport departed for Lakkavaram Reserve. ETA 21:30. Escort vehicle T-2, plus forest guard vehicle.

18:30 – Status update: TRANSPORT IN PROGRESS. All systems nominal.

19:15 – Radio check from escort: Sundari resting, no issues. Sedation wearing off as planned.

20:00 – Telemetry check: S-18 transmitting. Position moving along route.

21:15 – Arrived Lakkavaram Reserve. Release site pre-checked (20:00, fence intact, water source confirmed).

21:30 – Sundari released into soft-release enclosure (2 ha). She walked out of crate, explored perimeter, then settled under tree. Subadults not present – they will need to be monitored and possibly translocated later.

22:00 – STATUS CHANGE: CAPTURE COMPLETE. Sundari in soft-release enclosure at Lakkavaram Reserve. Monitoring schedule: hourly telemetry checks overnight, Dr. Meera on site.

22:30 – AR signs off. Notes: capture successful on second attempt. Bait-corral method effective. Subadult separation resolved naturally. Next steps: monitor Sundari 48 hrs, assess adaptation, then decide on subadult relocation.

### Agenda Item 3: Review of Incident Report – Near-Miss at Culvert Site (08 Aug)

Ravi opened the item by stating that the incident report from 8 August had been circulated to all leads earlier in the day. He asked the team to go through the key points together so that everyone is aligned before the road work resumes.

Imran summarized the incident for the record: On 8 August at approximately 11:40 hrs, a field crew vehicle (Gypsy, registration GJ-05-AB-4321) was returning from the north fence line when the rear wheel dropped into a soft patch on the approach to the culvert. The vehicle tilted but did not roll over. No injuries. Two fence posts (north-west section, markers N-14 and N-15) were damaged when the crew used a tow rope anchored to them to pull the vehicle out. The posts were temporarily braced the same afternoon.

Dr. Rao asked whether Sundari had shown any reaction to the incident. Imran said the observation blind log showed no change in behaviour for two hours after the noise. Dr. Rao noted in the margin of her copy: "No stress response observed, but the incident occurred near the culvert, which is within 300 m of the holding enclosure. Keep monitoring."

Ravi read out the formal findings from the report:

- **Root Cause:** Unmarked soft shoulder on the culvert approach, worsened by recent rain. The area had not been re-inspected after the last rainfall event.
- **Contributing Factor:** The crew did not halt to check the shoulder before crossing, despite a standing instruction to do so after rain.
- **Corrective Actions Taken Immediately:** Temporary bracing of posts N-14 and N-15; soft patch marked with red flags; vehicle crossing halted until further notice.
- **Recommendation:** Full repair of the culvert approach and shoulder before any vehicle movement resumes. Permanent signage to be installed.

Ravi asked for a vote on the recommendation. All present voted in favour of proceeding with the full repair. The motion was carried unanimously.

**Decision D-14-03:** The culvert approach and shoulder will be fully repaired before any vehicle movement resumes. Repair work will be scheduled for 16 August, weather permitting. The red flags will remain in place until the repair is completed.

Imran added that the damaged posts will be replaced as part of the fence reinforcement task (A-14-02), not just braced. Pooja confirmed that replacement posts are already in the storage shed and are the same specification as the originals.

11:15 – Visual observation from ridge (binoculars, ~400m). Sundari accompanied by two subadult males. Noted minor limp in left foreleg – likely old injury, no new wound. Vet (Dr. Meera) consulted remotely; advised no intervention unless limping worsens.

13:30 – Return to base. Vehicle T-2 tire pressure checked. All good.

14:20 – Radio message from Range Officer (Nallamala West): reported fresh pugmarks near Yadavalli, possibly male elephant. Noted for tomorrow's briefing.

15:00 – Equipment storage. Collar S-17 placed on charger (backup). S-14 left on bench for final calibration.

05:55 – Team assembly. Weather: overcast, 22°C, humidity high. Rain likely by afternoon.

09:15 – Crossing attempted. T-2 made it across; T-1 (still at base) not needed. Capture team on foot forded with equipment. All personnel safe.

10:30 – Visual contact. Sundari resting under banyan tree, ~300m from planned drive path. Subadults grazing nearby. No disturbance.

12:00 – Drive progressing. Sundari moved ~1.5 km west, towards clearing. Pace steady.

12:45 – Radio check. All teams in position. Dr. Meera at clearing, ready.

13:20 – Sundari entered Yadavalli clearing. Capture team closing in.

14:05 – STATUS CHANGE: INTERRUPTED.

Reason: Sudden thunderstorm with lightning. Operations halted for safety. All personnel retreated to vehicles. Sundari and subadults moved to dense cover at clearing edge. No injuries, no equipment loss.

14:30 – Storm passed. Resumed assessment. Sundari still in clearing, but agitated. Subadults separated – one moved north, one stayed with her.

15:00 – Decision: abort drive for today. Sundari too stressed after storm. Subadult separation complicates capture. Team to regroup at base, reassess tomorrow.

16:20 – Status update: INTERRUPTED. Notes: storm disruption, subadult separation, Sundari stress level high. Next action: monitor overnight, reassess 06:00, 10 Aug.

10 Aug 2026 (continued)

09:50 – Radio: Sundari stopped at stream crossing. Drinking. Team A holding position 200m behind. No stress indicators.

10:15 – Sundari crossed stream. Moving north-east now, away from planned capture zone. Team A adjusting.

10:40 – Subadult (north) started moving south, towards Sundari. Team B on alert.

11:05 – Subadult rejoined Sundari. Both moving together now. Good – separation resolved on its own.

11:30 – Sundari entered secondary clearing, ~4 ha, good visibility. Team A closing.

12:00 – STATUS: CAPTURE ATTEMPT IN PROGRESS. Sundari in clearing, subadults both with her. Dr. Meera reports calm behavior – feeding on grass, no agitation.

12:25 – Capture team moved in. Sundari stood up, alert. Team held position.

12:40 – Sundari moved to clearing edge, looked back at team, then walked into dense cover. Subadults followed. Capture attempt failed – no dart fired.

13:00 – Team regrouped. Discussion: Sundari aware of presence, but not fleeing far. She is holding territory, not stressed. Dr. Meera: "She knows we're here. She's not afraid, just cautious. We need a different approach."

13:30 – Decision: switch to bait-corral method. Use existing corral at Yadavalli clearing (checked 5 Aug, structure sound). Bait with fodder and minerals. Sundari has used this clearing before – familiar.

14:00 – Corral prep. Team B to Yadavalli. Team A to monitor Sundari from distance.

14:30 – Bait placed. Fodder, salt block, water. Corral gate left open, will close remotely.

15:00 – Sundari's position: 15.2480°N, 78.4665°E – moving slowly towards Yadavalli. Promising.

15:30 – Radio check. All teams in position. Dr. Meera at ridge, observing.

16:00 – Sundari at clearing edge, ~150m from corral. Feeding. Subadults nearby.

16:30 – Sundari entered corral. Gate closed remotely. SUCCESS. Capture complete.

16:45 – Vet team entered corral. Sundari sedated. Collar S-14 replaced with new GPS collar (S-18). Blood samples taken. Body condition good – weight 185 kg, no injuries.

17:15 – Subadults moved away from corral, into adjacent forest. Monitoring continues. They are not distressed – Dr. Meera observed them feeding within 30 min.

17:30 – Sundari loaded for transport. Vehicle T-3 (transport crate) confirmed ready.

18:00 – Transport departed for Lakkavaram Reserve. ETA 21:30. Escort vehicle T-2, plus forest guard vehicle.

18:30 – Status update: TRANSPORT IN PROGRESS. All systems nominal.

19:15 – Radio check from escort: Sundari resting, no issues. Sedation wearing off as planned.

20:00 – Telemetry check: S-18 transmitting. Position moving along route.

21:15 – Arrived Lakkavaram Reserve. Release site pre-checked (20:00, fence intact, water source confirmed).

21:30 – Sundari released into soft-release enclosure (2 ha). She walked out of crate, explored perimeter, then settled under tree. Subadults not present – they will need to be monitored and possibly translocated later.

22:00 – STATUS CHANGE: CAPTURE COMPLETE. Sundari in soft-release enclosure at Lakkavaram Reserve. Monitoring schedule: hourly telemetry checks overnight, Dr. Meera on site.

22:30 – AR signs off. Notes: capture successful on second attempt. Bait-corral method effective. Subadult separation resolved naturally. Next steps: monitor Sundari 48 hrs, assess adaptation, then decide on subadult relocation.

documents.title: Operations Meeting Minutes – Sundari Translocation Operation
documents.content:
The current status of the operation is formally noted as: **Interrupted – awaiting road repair.**

It was confirmed that all animals remain in the holding enclosure and are in stable condition. No further translocation attempts are to be made until the road is verified safe for the transport vehicle.

---

**2. Telemetry and Animal Health Update (for the record)**

Arjun Mehta presented the telemetry summary for the past seven days:

- Sundari (female, collared 03 August): Signal stable, collar battery at approx. 78%. No unusual movement patterns. She has been resting in the shaded corner of the enclosure, which Dr. Rao noted is normal behaviour for mid-day.
- The two cubs (approx. 8 months old) are not collared but are observed via camera trap. They are feeding well and staying close to the female.
- No signal loss was reported after the rain event. One minor gap occurred on 09 August for about 40 minutes due to cloud cover; no data anomalies.

Dr. Rao added a verbal note (informal) that Sundari has been slightly more vocal in the early mornings, which he attributes to the cooler weather and the nearby stream noise, not distress. He will monitor and will flag if the pattern changes.

---

Operations meeting minutes state the Sundari Translocation Operation next_priority is repair road and resume translocation. Record status: current.

**3. Discussion: Road Repair Options and Timeline**

Imran Khan presented the condition of the service road. The culvert at kilometre marker 4.2 has partially collapsed, leaving a gap of approximately 1.5 metres across the road surface. The surrounding soil is saturated, and the road base is unstable for the weight of the transport vehicle (approx. 6 tonnes fully loaded).

Three options were discussed:

**Option A – Temporary repair (gravel and timber matting)**
- Proposed by Imran. Estimated time: 1–2 days.
- Cost: low (material available at camp).
- Risk: moderate. The matting may not hold if further rain occurs. The transport vehicle would need to cross at slow speed, and a second inspection would be required before each crossing.

**Option B – Full culvert replacement (concrete pipe)**
- Proposed by Deepak Prasad (Road Crew Supervisor, joined the meeting at 10:20).
- Estimated time: 5–7 days, assuming dry weather and materials delivered from the district store.
- Cost: higher, but provides a long-term fix.
- Risk: low for the operation, but the delay is significant. The holding enclosure is adequate for the current period, but if the monsoon intensifies, the access road may worsen.

**Option C – Alternate route via the eastern ridge**
- Proposed by Sunita Devi, who noted that the old logging track on the eastern ridge is sometimes used by villagers. She has walked it recently and believes it is passable for a light vehicle, but not for the heavy transport truck.
- Estimated time: 2 days to clear vegetation, but the gradient is steep and the track is narrow. The transport vehicle would likely require a winch and escort.
- Risk: high. Not recommended for the crate vehicle.

**Team Discussion:**

Ravi asked each member for a brief view:
- Dr. Rao: Supports Option B for safety, but noted that the animals are healthy and can wait 5–7 days. He does not want to rush the move if the road is unsafe.
- Pooja Sharma: Concerned about the holding enclosure. She reported that the fence line on the north side has been tested by a wild boar twice this week. No breach, but she recommends reinforcing the two weak posts before any long delay.
- Arjun Mehta: No preference on the road, but requested that any repair work be scheduled for mornings so that telemetry checks are not interrupted.
- Imran Khan: Reiterated that Option A is the fastest and can be done with the current team, but he will not guarantee it if rain returns.
- Sunita Devi: Raised a community concern. Villagers from the nearby hamlet have been asking about the road closure. She suggested that a brief notice be put up at the village chowk explaining that repairs are underway, to avoid rumours about the operation.

Deepak Prasad clarified a point raised earlier: the district store has confirmed that 40 bags of cement and the required pipe sections can be delivered by 16 August, provided the access road from the main highway remains open. He also mentioned that the road crew has only one jackhammer in working condition; the second one has been out of service since May and parts have not arrived.

Sunita Devi asked whether the villagers' notice could be posted before the road decision was finalised. Ravi said it would be better to post the notice after the decision, so the message is accurate.

---

### Agenda Item 3: Review of Incident Report – Near-Miss at Culvert Site (08 Aug)

Ravi opened the item by stating that the incident report from 8 August had been circulated to all leads earlier in the day. He asked the team to go through the key points together so that everyone is aligned before the road work resumes.

Imran summarized the incident for the record: On 8 August at approximately 11:40 hrs, a field crew vehicle (Gypsy, registration GJ-05-AB-4321) was returning from the north fence line when the rear wheel dropped into a soft patch on the approach to the culvert. The vehicle tilted but did not roll over. No injuries. Two fence posts (north-west section, markers N-14 and N-15) were damaged when the crew used a tow rope anchored to them to pull the vehicle out. The posts were temporarily braced the same afternoon.

Dr. Rao asked whether Sundari had shown any reaction to the incident. Imran said the observation blind log showed no change in behaviour for two hours after the noise. Dr. Rao noted in the margin of her copy: "No stress response observed, but the incident occurred near the culvert, which is within 300 m of the holding enclosure. Keep monitoring."

Ravi read out the formal findings from the report:

- **Root Cause:** Unmarked soft shoulder on the culvert approach, worsened by recent rain. The area had not been re-inspected after the last rainfall event.
- **Contributing Factor:** The crew did not halt to check the shoulder before crossing, despite a standing instruction to do so after rain.
- **Corrective Actions Taken Immediately:** Temporary bracing of posts N-14 and N-15; soft patch marked with red flags; vehicle crossing halted until further notice.
- **Recommendation:** Full repair of the culvert approach and shoulder before any vehicle movement resumes. Permanent signage to be installed.

Ravi asked for a vote on the recommendation. All present voted in favour of proceeding with the full repair. The motion was carried unanimously.

**Decision D-14-03:** The culvert approach and shoulder will be fully repaired before any vehicle movement resumes. Repair work will be scheduled for 16 August, weather permitting. The red flags will remain in place until the repair is completed.

Imran added that the damaged posts will be replaced as part of the fence reinforcement task (A-14-02), not just braced. Pooja confirmed that replacement posts are already in the storage shed and are the same specification as the originals.

---

### Agenda Item 4: Communication Protocols During Road Repair

Ravi noted that the road repair work on 16 August will involve machinery and additional personnel. He asked the team to agree on how communication will be handled to avoid confusion and to keep the operation safe.

Imran proposed the following:

- All repair work will be coordinated through the base camp radio channel (Channel 2). The field crew will carry handheld radios at all times during the repair.
- The observation blind will have a dedicated radio operator (rotating from the WRU roster) to monitor Sundari's behaviour and to report immediately if she shows any sign of disturbance.
- Any vehicle movement on the road will be halted from 08:00 hrs until the repair is completed. Only foot movement will be allowed, and only via the marked footpath.
- The village headman will be informed in advance so that local traffic does not use the road during the repair window.
